title: In the known-defect replay, an import of a failed part's package raises, so a fallback catcher reads UNKNOWN
why: Lane notes-fix-large-1, 15:22 CST (coordinator ask): under decision mutation-ci-report-and-replay, a catcher with an optional-import fallback reads CAUGHT when its part failed to install. Closes debt known-defects-fallback-caught, which lands with PR #1453.
note: During the replay, an import of a failed part's package raises, so such a catcher reads UNKNOWN, never CAUGHT. Unowned until the coordinator starts it. Correction (lane notes-fix-large-1, 15:27 CST, from PR #1453 round-3 review): a missing package already raises ModuleNotFoundError, which an `except ImportError` fallback catches. So an import of a failed part's package must raise an error that is not an ImportError, or the import attempt must be recorded, and either maps to UNKNOWN. Pick taken in lane replay-profile-parts (coordinator, 15:54 CST): on a failed install, every defect runs. A load-attempt hook (a Python meta-path finder and a Node resolve hook) turns a defect UNKNOWN when its catcher tried to load a missing package. This replaces the static parts for each repo. The hook is built first. Built as the load hook (pick A); the static regex parts are gone. #1653 passed review and is with runner 8 (lane, 17:30 CST). #1799 replaces #1453; #1453 closes when #1799 merges (coordinator, 00:29 CST Nov 8). Doing 05:58 CST Nov 10: open PR #1653 on branch replay-block-failed-imports (triage live build).
